premises.text: With millions of photos shared daily across services, finding pictures you like is hard
premises.evidence_span: The question is, how do you find pictures you like?

premises.text: Skyline collects personal interests from social networks (liked pages, saved searches, hashtags, places) beyond just people
premises.evidence_span: We connect to your social networks to collect your interests

premises.text: Matching those interests to a real-time multi-service photo stream gives each user a personal skyline timeline (rank, friends, location, events, explore, back channel)
premises.evidence_span: Matching your personal interest to that stream of real-time photos means everybody gets his own skyline

premises.text: Product ships as website plus iPhone and Android apps with the same interest-based skylines
premises.evidence_span: We are not only launching this as a website, but also as an app, both on iPhone and on Android

premises.text: Brands can target an interest combined with location or time; site widgets share ad revenue or pay a monthly ad-free fee; services sit on an open API
premises.evidence_span: Brands can target an interest, like TechCrunch Disrupt, if they want, combined with location or time

value.text: Everyone gets a personal real-time stream of photos matched to their interests
value.evidence_span: everybody gets his own skyline, hence the company name Skylines

causal_links.evidence_span: how do you find pictures you like? That's where we come in
Matching your personal interest to that stream of real-time photos means everybody gets his own skyline
This both increases our revenue and our reach

notes: Picture-rank/friends/location/events/explore/back-channel folded as cascade of one interest-matched stream (§4.1.7). Interest collection kept with matching as one mechanism; multi-surface website/apps kept as distribution facet of product. Brand targeting+widget monetization separately revisable. Singleton D1/D3 justified as problem vs commercial modules.
